This guide walks one analysis from a `lavaan` fit to a reported result, and says what to check at each step.
It uses the same simulated data as [Two-level mediation](model-twolevel.html), which is the reference page for
every option; read that page when a step here needs more detail. The route needs `lavaan` (Suggests).

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
has_lavaan <- requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)
```

## Step 1: fit the same regressions at both levels

Treatment, mediator and outcome are measured on level-1 units nested in clusters. Write the same three
regressions at `level: 1` (within) and `level: 2` (between) and fit with `cluster =`.

```{r}
#| label: data
set.seed(2026)
J <- 100
n <- 5
id <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n)
xb <- rnorm(J)[id]
xw <- rnorm(J * n)
x <- xb + xw
m <- 0.4 * xw + 0.7 * xb + 0.5 * rnorm(J)[id] + rnorm(J * n)
mbar <- ave(m, id)
y <- 0.3 * xw + 0.2 * xb + 0.5 * (m - mbar) + 0.9 * mbar + 0.5 * rnorm(J)[id] + rnorm(J * n)
d <- data.frame(id = id, X = x, M = m, Y = y)

model <- "
  level: 1
    M ~ X
    Y ~ M + X
  level: 2
    M ~ X
    Y ~ M + X
"
```

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
fit <- lavaan::sem(model, data = d, cluster = "id")
```

## Step 2: extract, then check the fit before reading any effect

`extract_mediation()` reads the fit and never refits. Name the three roles; the paths are found by variable
name and level, not by label.

```{r}
#| label: extract
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
td <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")
```

Three properties decide whether the between-level numbers can be trusted. Read them first.

```{r}
#| label: checks
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
td@icc
td@between_identified
td@admissible
td@n_clusters
td@cross_level_equal
```

| Check | What it means | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| `between_identified` | the treatment and the mediator vary enough between clusters (ICC at least 0.01) | only the within effects are returned; between effects and the contrast stop with class `medfit_between_unidentified` |
| `admissible` | lavaan's post-check passed (no negative variance) | inspect the fit; standard errors on a negative variance are `NA` with a `medfit_warning_vcov_diagonal` warning |
| `n_clusters` | fewer than 50 clusters triggers a warning (a judgment, not a published cutoff) | treat between results as rough |
| `cross_level_equal` | paths constrained equal across levels (`a`, `b`, or both) | with both equated the contrast is `NA` by constraint |

## Step 3: read the effects at each level

```{r}
#| label: effects
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
nie(td)
nie(td, level = "between")
tidy(td, conf_int = TRUE)
```

The within and between indirect effects are separate quantities: $a_w b_w$ and $a_b b_b$. Standard errors use
the delta method over the joint covariance, so the covariance between a within and a between slope is part of
every one. The intervals are Wald intervals.

## Step 4: treat the contrast as descriptive

`nie(td, level = "contrast")` is the within effect minus the between effect. It is returned unless both `a`
and `b` are equated across levels. It describes a difference between two quantities; it is not a test that
the levels differ.

```{r}
#| label: contrast
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
nie(td, level = "contrast")
```

## Step 5: choose an interval

The delta-method interval from Step 3 is the default. When you want a distribution-based interval, use the
cluster bootstrap: pass the `lavaan` fit to `twolevel_statistic()` and give `bootstrap_mediation()` the data
and `cluster =`. Whole clusters are resampled and the model is refitted in every replicate. The example uses 30
replicates only to keep the page fast; use several hundred in a real analysis.

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
b <- bootstrap_mediation(
  twolevel_statistic(fit, "nie_between", treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y"),
  method = "nonparametric", data = d, cluster = "id", n_boot = 30, seed = 1
)
c(estimate = b@estimate, lower = b@ci_lower, upper = b@ci_upper, n_used = b@n_boot)
```

Report the percentile interval (`ci_lower`, `ci_upper`), not the standard deviation of the draws: refits with a
negative between variance are kept, and at a few dozen clusters they give heavy tails. Replicates that fail
are excluded and counted in a warning, so check `n_boot` in the result.

## Step 6: report

State, at minimum: the number of clusters and the cluster sizes; the ICC of the treatment and the mediator;
whether the fit was admissible; the within and between indirect effects with their intervals and the interval
type; and, if you give the contrast, that it is descriptive. `summary(td)` prints the provenance of the fit and
the assumptions in full.

```{r}
#| label: summary
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
glance(td)
```

## When something goes wrong

Each condition carries a class. The [Troubleshooting guide](guide-troubleshooting.html#two-level-mediation)
lists every two-level message with its cause and fix, and [Which interval should I use?](guide-intervals.html)
compares the interval types.
